title: Qwen3 PD inference
speaker_notes_en: Our task is to serve Qwen3-235B on sixteen H200 GPUs with disaggregated prefill and decode. Each request contains about 4000 input tokens and produces 200 output tokens. We optimise the serving configuration and KV-transfer path while retaining the published FP8 model computation.

title: Performance at N48
speaker_notes_en: The selected configuration reaches 1912.30 good output tokens per second at concurrency 48. A total of 97.44% of requests satisfy both latency limits. This is a 14.78% end-to-end improvement over our previous best configuration. The gain combines topology, concurrency and transport changes.

title: The latency gate
text: ≥ 90% of requests must pass both. Errors stay in the denominator.
speaker_notes_en: Goodput is determined per request. Time to the first token must be at most 3000 milliseconds, and the average interval between output tokens must be at most 20 milliseconds. At least 90% of requests must meet both limits. Increasing raw throughput alone is insufficient.

title: Two nodes. Sixteen H200 GPUs.
speaker_notes_en: The platform has two nodes with eight H200 GPUs each, connected through InfiniBand NDR. We use the official FP8 checkpoint and BF16 KV cache. SGLang provides inference and NIXL provides cross-node KV transfer. No tensor-parallel group spans both nodes.

title: Winning topology: TP4 prefill → TP8 / EP8 decode
text: Winning topology: TP4 prefill → TP8 / EP8 decode
speaker_notes_en: The selected topology uses two four-GPU prefill workers on the first node and one eight-GPU decode worker on the second. Prefill uses TP4/EP1; decode uses TP8/EP8. There are two possible KV-transfer paths. Every request is prefilled on a prefill worker and decoded on the decode worker.

title: From the provided layouts to the selected split
text: From the provided layouts to the selected split
speaker_notes_en: The starting layout has four TP2 prefill workers and two TP4/EP4 decode workers. Widening prefill to TP4 reduces the number of replicas to two. The selected layout also widens decode to TP8/EP8. These choices trade replica count for parallelism within each request, so we compare them under the latency gate.

title: Seventeen usable layouts measured
text: All layouts: N16 / N32 / N40 / N48
speaker_notes_en: We explore seventeen usable arrangements across 8+8, 4+12 and 12+4 GPU splits. We vary tensor parallelism and test concurrency 16, 32, 40 and 48. Fourteen originals and three distinct EP2 replacements are measured. The original TP8/EP1 layouts cannot load the FP8 block geometry and remain separate from their replacements.

title: Benchmark protocol
text: Initialise workers  →  warm P/D paths  →  sustain N48
Only this window contributes to goodput.
Closed loop: completion immediately triggers the next request, sustaining N48.
speaker_notes_en: We initialise the serving workers and all P/D connections before benchmarking. The official client performs 60 seconds of warmup, 120 seconds of measurement and 30 seconds of grace. The workload is closed-loop: each completed request is immediately replaced, sustaining the chosen concurrency.

title: Load selection: N48 passes the short sweep
text: Load selection: N48 passes the short sweep
speaker_notes_en: The short sweep shows throughput rising with concurrency, while the fraction satisfying both SLAs decreases. At N48, the selected layout still passes the 90% gate. We use short runs to screen settings, then confirm the selected operating point with the full measurement duration.

title: Long-run comparison: +14.78% over the previous best
text: Long-run comparison: +14.78% over the previous best
Topology, concurrency and transport changed; this is an end-to-end gain.
speaker_notes_en: All bars show long measurements on the same sixteen-GPU platform. The selected TP4-to-TP8/EP8 layout reaches 1912.30 good tokens per second, compared with 1666.01 for the previous best. The alternative TP8/EP2 layout is slower. These comparisons measure the complete configuration rather than isolate the patch alone.

title: Per-request latency: 1,180 of 1,211 pass both limits
text: Per-request latency: 1,180 of 1,211 pass both limits

TTFT mean 1,482 ms
ITL mean 16.79 ms
speaker_notes_en: The scatter plot shows time to first token and mean inter-token latency for each request. Of 1211 requests, 1180 meet both limits. Thirty-one miss a limit; no request errors or cancellations occurred. The distribution matters because aggregate averages alone cannot establish the 90% gate.

title: Cold KV-transfer setup
text:
Pair warmup timed out.
Measurement could not begin.

Workers ready at 269s.
All P/D paths warm at 303s.
Four sweeps + long N32.
Connection setup is separate from the measured latency window.
speaker_notes_en: Cold KV-transfer setup can stall before the measured workload begins. The original path timed out after 480 seconds. With request-scoped descriptor preparation, workers were ready at 269 seconds and all P/D paths were warm at 303 seconds. Those timestamps include worker and connection setup, not just the KV copy. The benchmark latency thresholds are unchanged.

title: FP8 block alignment requires a distinct EP2 variant
text: FP8 block alignment requires a distinct EP2 variant
speaker_notes_en: FP8 quantisation uses 128-wide blocks. TP8/EP1 creates 192-wide expert shards, leaving a partial block. EP2 distributes experts into two groups and gives effective TP4, creating 384-wide shards that fit exactly three blocks. All experts and weights are retained; this is a different parallelism configuration, not model pruning.

title: NIXL: describe the request, not the whole KV pool
text: NIXL: describe the request, not the whole KV pool
Example: TP8 source, 94 layers, 4,000 contiguous tokens. Byte-range checks: 720 + 936 cases.
speaker_notes_en: The original NIXL path prepares descriptors for the entire KV pool. Our patch prepares them for the request pages instead. For the illustrated TP8-source geometry, the full pool contains about 403.8 million source entries per rank, whereas a contiguous 4000-token request can be coalesced to 188 entries. Head mapping, byte ranges and notifications are preserved. The two transport paths passed 720 and 936 CPU range comparisons and served GPU benchmarks.

title: Latency headroom at N48
text: Mean latency relative to the per-request limits
Decode latency is closer to its limit; more load reduces headroom.
speaker_notes_en: At N48, the mean time to first token is about 1482 milliseconds against a 3000-millisecond limit. Mean ITL is 16.79 milliseconds against a 20-millisecond limit. Decode latency is closer to its threshold. These means illustrate headroom; the actual acceptance decision remains per request and is shown by the distribution.

title: Latency and accuracy are separate acceptance checks
text: Latency and accuracy are separate acceptance checks

Passing local measurement
Required: at least 90%

Full-set output-quality checks
Target: ≥99% of reference
FP8 weights remain unchanged
speaker_notes_en: Latency and output quality are separate checks. The selected configuration passes the latency gate. We retain the published FP8 weights, BF16 KV and the same model computation. Full-set accuracy evaluation against the organisers reference remains the next validation step; we do not claim that it is already complete.

title: Selected operating point
text: N48  ·  16 H200  ·  97.44% SLA  ·  request-scoped NIXL descriptors
speaker_notes_en: The selected operating point is two TP4 prefill workers, one TP8/EP8 decode worker and concurrency 48. It delivers 1912.30 good output tokens per second with 97.44% of requests satisfying both SLAs. The key changes are the parallelism balance and request-scoped KV descriptor preparation.

title: Appendix · alternative TP8 / EP2 prefill
speaker_notes_en: This alternative uses TP8/EP2 prefill and TP8/EP8 decode. Its N40 and N48 sweeps fail the 90% gate despite higher throughput. Long N32 passes with 1507.96 good tokens per second and 95.38% SLA, so it is viable but slower than the selected layout.

title: Discussion
speaker_notes_en: Invite questions about tensor and expert parallelism, the KV-transfer optimisation, and throughput under the latency constraints. Explain that all sixteen GPUs are used, the model computation is retained, and the full-set accuracy check is still outstanding.
